area: Critique of the demo and video ideas (A generic notebook tour, B Playground Feature-tour in three hosts, C NucleiSky 2D recorded-values demo, D two-minute video + homepage tile): lead example, staging, honesty, drift, accessibility, privacy, scope.

findings:
VERDICT IN ONE PARAGRAPH
Do not build the proposal as specified (three high-fidelity re-drawn desktop applications plus a 2-minute video that covers the whole product). The facts say the honest, shippable core is much smaller: NucleiSky 2D in the NOTEBOOK only, shown through REAL, dated captures of the installed app plus one genuinely interactive but non-fabricated element (a viewer over recorded real outputs). napari and Fiji views should be a later stage that is gated on facts outside the site repo (NucleiSky main shipping tools, a release, host validation on a real desktop). The video should be split by audience and shortened. Everything the visitor can touch must either be a real control (native input/button that changes a real image) or be absent.

1. WHICH EXAMPLE SHOULD LEAD, AND WHY
Lead with NucleiSky 2D, notebook only. Reasons:
- Honesty: it is the only candidate whose released product (0.1.1, installers for 3 OS, manifest 'hosts: [notebook]') matches what is shown. Idea B (Playground Feature tour in three hosts) and spec C's napari/Fiji tabs depict things that are not in the shipped NucleiSky (tools only on bridge-test) or not in any notebook (Feature tour has no notebook cell). Showing them as equal tabs asserts parity the repos deny (HOST_PARITY.md: 71 of 164 rows DIVERGES; the guide says 'untested and unlikely to be stable').
- Self-explanation: the 'constellation' metaphor (match the pattern of nuclei like stars) is understood in seconds and is already the app's own tagline on the site.
- Citation: the paper (jcs.265152) is already in the manifest and on the app page.
- Against NucleiSky: the fixture is synthetic Gaussian blobs (n_query=9), real nuclei exist only in 2D_QC.jpg of unknown provenance. Remedy: ask the NucleiSky authors (they are the paper's authors) for one small real field image with a licence, and use the notebook's own 'Generate Random Crop' with fixed seed: the crop is cut from the reference by the app, so the true transform is known and the displayed error can be computed from a real run. Until then use the fixture and label it 'synthetic test image' in the caption.
- Why not Idea B first: Playground sits in the site's 'Testing and maintenance' section, the image is flat discs, the threshold slider is inert over about 75 % of its range (plateau 0.05-0.76 per earlier investigation), there are no real captures, and the notebook view does not exist. It is, however, the only app whose released build ships host tools on main, so it is the right candidate for the Stage 3 host views once real desktop captures exist.
- Why not Idea A as written: the 'select reference image, Generate Random Crop, Run' tour is faithful in spirit but the five-step structure in the ideas file is not the real notebook (Steps 0-3, segmentation as its own run, Options A/B). Keep A's constraints (honest label, no uploads, no JupyterLite) and its placement advice; replace its simulated notebook with real frames.

2. DOES THE NOTEBOOK-FIRST STORY COME BEFORE THE HOST VIEWS?
Yes, and the host views should not be tabs of equal rank. The site's claim is 'notebooks in, desktop apps out' (data/site.yaml hero) and the home page already says 'Soon, apps can also work inside napari, Fiji and QuPath'. A host tab next to Notebook invites the reading 'napari/Fiji work today'. In Stage 1 hosts get one sentence and a link to the existing /guides/image-software/ page. In Stage 3, if shown at all, use real screenshots (not re-drawn), one per host, labelled 'prototype capture' inside the figure frame.

3. DEPENDENCY ON AN EXPERIMENTAL BRIDGE
The demo should not depend on it. The Fiji path alone is multi-dialog, uses one or two chooser dialogs before the form (prior investigation, not re-run by me), and Fiji macro recording does not work (Tools docs). The bridge docs disagree with each other on several points (HOST_PARITY). Anything quoted from them goes stale quickly. Dependencies are acceptable only as outbound links to the guides the site already imports.

4. SMALLEST LAUNCH-WORTHY VERSION
One page /demo/ (or even just the app page) containing: one-sentence task; a stepper of 5 to 6 REAL frames from installed NucleiSky 0.1.1 (open app icon, Welcome notebook, Open the notebook, load images, run, result) with captions and a caption stamp; one recorded-run image viewer with real native controls (checkboxes for reference/query/aligned overlay, an opacity range input); a persistent note that results are recorded; citation from the manifest; links to install and the guide. No video, no hosts, no simulated Run button. This needs: a tiny script, a narrow check_design allowance (tabs/range/checkbox in a data-demo root), and tests. It fully serves the 'newcomer understands the task and how LabConstrictor makes it accessible' goal without any re-drawn UI.

5. SHIP TOGETHER OR IN STAGES
In stages with gates (section 14). The demo and video have different readers (a biologist trying an app vs a developer evaluating the framework) and different decay rates. Shipping the video first with real captures is cheap and low-risk for a user audience but it cannot be updated as the product changes; ship it after the stills exist so it reuses them.

6. WHERE THE VIDEO ADDS VALUE, WHERE IT DUPLICATES
Adds: motion that stills cannot show (double-click app icon, browser opens JupyterLab by itself, the code is hidden, a run takes a visible number of seconds), the 'installer builds in the cloud from a GitHub release' sequence, and narration of why. Duplicates: anything the demo already shows (the registration result, the notebook UI, the host forms) and anything the docs already say in text (notebook portability rules, requirements.yaml, manifest fields).
Is the 2-minute cut too much? Yes. Evidence: 260-300 words of narration for eight topics (per-segment word budgets in the facts). The host segment cannot honestly say 'optional, untested, napari and Fiji' and show it in 17 s. The storyboard also mixes two audiences and two call-to-actions. It says 'API design is a recommended practice, not mandatory', which is a developer message that biologists will not need.
Alternative cut:
- Video A, users (60 to 90 s): problem (colleague cannot run your script) -> download the installer -> open the app (browser opens) -> Welcome notebook -> run one analysis -> result -> where to find apps (App Centre). No host integration, no API talk. Uses the same real frames as the demo.
- Video B, builders (90 to 120 s, later, only if A is used): notebook -> template -> release builds installers -> labconstrictor-app.yaml and submit. State 'reusable package and optional napari/Fiji tools' as one end-card sentence with a link, not a segment.
Keep both silent-capable (captions burned or .vtt) so that mute viewing works. Narration only if tooling exists; do not block on it.

7. MAINTENANCE DRIFT OF THIRD-PARTY UIs
- Re-drawn mock-ups of JupyterLab, napari and Fiji are three look-alikes that will rot silently; the reference screenshots already predate the current widget (earlier investigation: no 'Copy as command', 'Details...' ellipsis difference, no points/outline layers, app/tool preselected) and are Linux/Xvfb captures with napari 0.9.2 PyQt5 (PyQt5 backend to be removed in fall 2026 per the clean-test report's own deprecation notice quote).
- Prefer captures, stamped: each figure caption carries 'NucleiSky 0.1.1 - JupyterLab x.y - Windows 11 - captured YYYY-MM-DD'. The stamp is data (a small YAML beside the images), not prose.
- Make staleness machine-visible without new manual work: build_site already holds the app's latest release tag in the snapshot (nucleisky 0.1.1, 2026-07-07). A check compares the captured version to the snapshot; when they differ the page shows a derived line 'Captured with 0.1.1; the latest release is X' and the build writes a named warning to build/problems.md (no silent fallback). A host-app version change cannot be detected, so also show the date and set a 6-month review date in the stamp file; the check warns after it passes.
- Never show a Windows window chrome or browser UI the lab does not control; crop to the app content.
- The demo must not carry a second description of the bridge (the 6-step collapsible duplicates LabConstrictor-Tools docs and the imported /guides/image-software/ guide, and one step, installer registration, is false for the template main today). Link instead.

8. RISK OF A HIGH-FIDELITY IMITATION SUGGESTING VALIDATION
The more convincing the napari/Fiji replica, the more it reads as 'this is available'. Mitigations:
- Do not replicate host chrome at all; use real captures.
- Where the label sits: inside the figure frame (a band at the top of the image, part of the same element so it survives cropping and screenshots), plus in the tab/figure heading itself ('napari - prototype'), not only in a caption underneath. On phones the band sits above the image, not below the fold.
- Wording: use the bridge's own sentence, 'untested and unlikely to be stable', not 'Experimental integration - currently under testing'. The shorter label understates; the site's Ecosystem copy and the Tools guide use the stronger one.
- No 'works in napari/Fiji' on the NucleiSky App Centre page: NucleiSky's manifest says hosts [notebook] and /apps/nucleisky/ has zero 'Soon in' chips (grep count 0), while Playground's page has one. A demo that shows NucleiSky in Fiji contradicts the site's own app page.
- Third-party names and logos: the site footer says logos are 'shown only to identify them'. A re-drawn napari window with its icon goes beyond identification; I could not read napari's or Fiji's mark terms: unverified.

9. ACCESSIBILITY TRAPS OF A SIMULATED DESKTOP
- A fake window that contains fake menus (File Edit View ...), fake toolbar icons and tabs creates dozens of tab stops and announcements that do nothing; aria-hidden does not help when the content is focusable (axe 'aria-hidden-focus'). Decide per element: either it is a real control with a real effect and an accessible name, or it is non-interactive and not focusable. Cleaner: no fake window; real images with real alt text and a short text description of what is visible, and the real controls (checkboxes, range) outside the image.
- Tabs for Notebook/napari/Fiji need role=tablist/tab/tabpanel, aria-selected, aria-controls, roving tabindex and arrow keys; a stepper (ordered list + Previous/Next native buttons) is simpler and needs less. Only one tab should be selected in static HTML (also for no-JS).
- Status ('Running', 'Complete') needs one polite live region; do not animate a fake progress bar (honesty and reduced motion). With prefers-reduced-motion nothing should animate.
- Reading order: the DOM order must follow the visual order; simulated panels must not be h1-h6 (heading-order checks and search index; earlier site-fit work found the simulated menus would enter search.json without data-search-exclude).
- Contrast: faithful napari greys on dark and Fiji grey dialogs can fail WCAG 1.4.3; I did not measure them (unverified). Fidelity and legibility conflict; screenshots avoid the conflict because they carry a text alternative.
- Mobile: a scaled-down desktop is unreadable at 390 px; use the image + caption stack. The simulated-window approach also duplicates the 'mobile layout not a miniature desktop' requirement the spec itself states.

10. PRIVACY: VIDEO HOSTING
- Verified: the home page and an app page make requests only to the site origin (Playwright: 33/29 requests, all localhost:8765). Fonts are self-hosted (mkdocs.yml:15).
- A YouTube embed (even youtube-nocookie) loads a Google player on page load, which discloses the visitor's IP to a third party and contradicts the spec's own 'no external scripts' (general knowledge, not tested here). It would also be the first external request the site makes.
- Recommended: self-hosted MP4 (H.264, AAC if audio), <video controls preload=\"none\" poster>, a <track kind=captions>, a visible transcript, no autoplay. A plain outbound link 'Also on YouTube' is acceptable and costs no tracking on the page itself. Size: earlier site-fit measurement says about 3 MB for a mostly static 1080p screencast and about 12 MB with continuous zoom/pan (not re-measured by me); restrained motion matters. Repeated re-encodes grow git history, so commit the final MP4 once and regenerate rarely; keep sources and the script in the repo, not the intermediate renders.
- The site is currently unlisted (listed: false), so a YouTube copy is the only discoverable channel at present: that is a launch decision for the lab, not a technical one.

11. VALIDITY OF 'A NEWCOMER SHOULD UNDERSTAND THE MICROSCOPY TASK AND HOW LABCONSTRICTOR MAKES IT ACCESSIBLE'
Two claims fused. Registration of a crop in a larger image is a niche task: many biologists will understand it only through the picture, and their understanding of NucleiSky is not evidence they understood LabConstrictor. The demo, as spec'd, shows the NucleiSky workflow; the distinctive LabConstrictor facts (installer, app in the start menu, the browser opens JupyterLab, code hidden, runs on your computer) appear only in passing. Separate the two outcomes.
Test with 5 biologists (usability test, not statistics; n=5 finds misreadings, cannot estimate rates):
- Recruit people who have never used LabConstrictor, at least two who have never opened Jupyter. Do not coach. Think-aloud, 5 minutes on the page, then no more than 6 questions in fixed wording.
- Q1 in your own words, what does the example do? (pass: 'finds where a small image sits in a big one' or equivalent). Q2 Where does the calculation run: this website, the cloud, or your computer? (pass: the installed app on their computer; fail: the website). Q3 Did the demo just analyse your data or a real image? (pass: no, recorded example). Q4 Could you use this with your own images tomorrow? What would you need to do? (pass: install, use own images, pixel size). Q5 Does this work in napari/Fiji today? (pass: not yet/uncertain; fail: yes). Q6 What would you click next?
- Pre-registered gate: at least 4 of 5 pass Q1 and Q2; 0 of 5 fail Q3 or Q5 (any fail means the wording or layout is changed and the test rerun with fresh participants). Record time-to-first-interaction (target 30 to 60 s as the spec says) and any control a participant tried to use that did nothing.
- Add a control: show two participants only the home-page tile and its text, and ask Q3 and Q5, to learn whether the tile alone over-promises.
- Also test on a phone (390 px) with one participant.

12. SCOPE CREEP VERSUS STANDING RULES
- The spec touches at least: pages_demo.py (new), build_site.py, config.py, pages_site.py, hubs.yaml, mkdocs.yml, DESIGN.md, AGENTS.md, check_design.py (plus a new check module), page.py and check_site.py (poster attribute fix), demo.js, demo.css, tests, content assets. A single feature that edits the design gate and the inventory rules is a signal; the check_design change must be narrow and bound to a data-demo root with its own failure test, or the feature will weaken a gate.
- 'Single source of truth' and 'no second manually maintained description': the demo restates NucleiSky parameter names, host form labels, the six-step bridge flow, the DOI text and fixture values by hand. Each must come from a file (manifest, snapshot, a provenance YAML beside the assets) or be dropped.
- 'Author-controlled exposure': the demo is the site's own description of NucleiSky, not the app author's. NucleiSky's authors should be asked first (and NucleiSky's manifest `screenshots` already supports captioned images; adding three real frames there needs no site code and puts the author in control).
- 'No silent fallbacks': a demo that quietly falls back to a static image when JS fails is fine only if that is the designed no-JS state and is tested; a missing asset must fail the build with the file named.
- JS/CSS have no size gate (lc.css is 338 lines): decide an explicit budget in DESIGN.md rather than relying on convention.
- Video adds a binary to the repo and an authoring chain (ffmpeg, captions) the repo has none of; keep sources and a regenerate script, and do not add dependencies to requirements.txt.
- Estimated effort is unverified, but Stage 1 is days; the spec's three fidelity-matched windows plus bridge states plus video is weeks and mostly spent on the part that decays.

13. RELATION TO OTHER PENDING WORK
- App Centre per-app 'input -> output example': the planned optional manifest fields (inputs, outputs, limitations, quickstart, screenshots with captions) are the scalable form of the same idea and are author-controlled. The NucleiSky /demo/ should be built so that it is the 'rich' version of what that mechanism shows for every app: same captured-frames-with-stamps pattern; the demo reads NucleiSky's own entries instead of a private data file where possible.
- Docs 'run an example' tutorial: the same captured frames should appear in the tutorial, not be re-captured; one set of stamped frames serves the tutorial, the demo and the video. Put the frames and their stamp file in one folder that all three read.
- Citation: the demo must cite the NucleiSky paper, read from the manifest 'doi' (already rendered as a 'Cite' row by pages_apps.py:152-153), kept visibly separate from the LabConstrictor citation (data/site.yaml citation_doi 10.5281/zenodo.20758747). Pending citation work (planning/results/3-citation) also flags the NucleiSky banner/logo provenance; do not use the banner as a scientific image in the demo.
- Do not duplicate the 'Cite' or 'Works with' content as hand-written text in /demo/.

14. RECOMMENDED STAGING WITH GO/NO-GO GATES
Stage 0, 'Capture the truth' (no site feature). Install NucleiSky 0.1.1 on a clean real Windows or macOS machine by someone other than its developer; capture the six frames and a recorded run (preferably with the app's Generate Random Crop and a fixed seed on an owner-approved real image); store the result image, the transform values the app printed, the app and OS versions and the date; fix the Welcome-picture alt text on the Use hub. Optionally add the frames to NucleiSky's manifest `screenshots`.
Gate G0 (go if all): captured on a real desktop, not Xvfb; the numbers shown are exactly those the run printed; the image licence or the fixture label is settled; NucleiSky maintainers agreed to be shown.
Stage 1, 'Honest viewer'. /demo/ with stepper of real frames + recorded-run viewer (checkbox layers, opacity) + manifest-derived citation + disclosure; home tile as a third card beside the two existing entry cards (the hero already has two cards: 'I want to find an app', 'I want to make an app'; a tile should not outrank them, so label it as a secondary link) ; link from Use hub next to the Welcome picture and from the NucleiSky page. No host views, no video.
Gate G1 (go if all): 5-biologist test passes the pre-registered thresholds above; Playwright test asserts zero external requests, keyboard-only walk-through, reduced motion, 390 px with no horizontal scroll; check_design/check_site/tests green with the narrow rule and its failure test; staleness check demonstrably fires on a fake newer release.
Stage 2, 'Video for users' (60 to 90 s, self-hosted, captions, transcript, poster). Built from Stage 0 frames. Gate G2: every on-screen label matches current docs; captions match narration; works without JS and on a phone; size under an agreed cap (suggest under 10 MB); no autoplay; the transcript is a derivative of existing docs wording, with a review date.
Stage 3, 'Host views' (conditional, may never happen). Preconditions outside this repo: NucleiSky main ships its lc_tools and a release, its manifest says hosts include napari/fiji, the bridge's guide status is raised from 'untested and unlikely to be stable', and the views were captured on a real Windows or macOS desktop. Gate G3: those four preconditions, plus the site's app page chips agree. Otherwise only link to /guides/image-software/.
Stage 4 (optional), builders' video B.

15. WHAT I COULD NOT SETTLE
- Real-data image licence and provenance, owner consent, and whether the napari trademark/logo can be reproduced.
- Real-desktop appearance of napari/Fiji/JupyterLab on Windows/macOS.
- Whether VLab4Mic ships tools on main (clone looks partial).
- YouTube request behaviour and Pages bandwidth limits (general knowledge only).
risks: Overclaim: a polished napari/Fiji tab beside Notebook implies parity and availability for NucleiSky; its manifest says hosts [notebook], tools exist only on bridge-test, and the bridge guide itself says 'untested and unlikely to be stable'.

Credential look-alike: a faithful Welcome notebook contains a GitHub personal-access-token flow (Welcome.ipynb:21, 598); a fake window with such a field could receive a real token. Omit it and say so.

Fabrication by accident: pairing the synthetic fixture inputs with 2D_QC.jpg (different dataset, SSIM=0.305 headline), or showing 'scale 1.0024' beside a 2x magnification, or showing 'done in 12.0 s' as a live duration.

Staleness: three re-drawn third-party UIs, plus a 2-minute video narrating button names and workflow order, decay faster than the site's other content; Linux/Xvfb references already predate the current widget.
Single-source violations: hard-coded DOI text, host labels, bridge steps (one false for template main), fixture numbers; a vendored copy of another repo's behaviour.
Gate erosion: broadening check_design button/alt rules to make the demo pass; an unscoped exemption would leak to other pages.
Accessibility: dozens of non-functional focusable fake controls, tab semantics done wrong, animated progress, low-contrast dark UI replicas, a miniature desktop at 390 px.
Privacy regression: first-ever third-party request if a YouTube iframe is used; also contradicts the spec's own 'no external scripts'.
Audience mismatch: one video for biologists and builders satisfies neither; 260-300 words cannot carry eight topics; host segment would be rushed into either an overclaim or a caveat nobody can read.
Launch dependency: site is unlisted (listed: false) and the App Centre it advertises is not indexed; the video's call to action points at a site search engines cannot see.
Image provenance: NucleiSky banner/logo carry a generative-AI sparkle and Gemini filenames; the unresolved provenance (planning/results/3-citation) means they should not appear in a scientific demo.
A bespoke NucleiSky-only demo does not scale to other apps and competes with the planned per-app inputs/outputs/quickstart fields; effort could duplicate the App Centre work.
Test validity: n=5 cannot estimate comprehension rates; a pass on 'understood the task' says nothing about 'understood LabConstrictor' unless questions separate them.
recommendations: Adopt the staged plan: Stage 0 real captures on a real desktop; Stage 1 notebook-only honest viewer; Stage 2 short users' video; Stage 3 host views only after external preconditions; builders' video optional. Each stage has the go/no-go gate in the findings.

Lead example: NucleiSky 2D, notebook only. Prefer the app's own 'Generate Random Crop' with fixed seed on an owner-approved real image so the ground truth is known and any displayed error is computed from a real run; otherwise use the fixture labelled 'synthetic test image'. Keep Playground Feature tour for the later host stage.

Interactivity without fabrication: a stepper of real frames plus a recorded-run viewer with native checkboxes and an opacity range input; no simulated Run button, no sliders that cannot recompute. Remove or label any control with no effect.

Do not re-draw napari, Fiji or JupyterLab. Use stamped real captures ('NucleiSky 0.1.1 - OS - captured date'), and derive a staleness notice and a named build warning by comparing the stamp to the snapshot's latest release.

Host label: put it inside the figure frame and in the heading, with the bridge's own words ('untested and unlikely to be stable'); do not show NucleiSky in napari/Fiji until its manifest and main branch say so.

Split the video: 60 to 90 s for users (install, open, run, result, App Centre); a separate, later builders' video; host integration as a single end-card sentence with a link. Budget narration at about 130 to 150 wpm and trim to fit; captions and transcript always.
Self-host the MP4 with controls, poster, captions, no autoplay; at most an outbound 'Also on YouTube' link. Commit the final encode once.
Read the NucleiSky citation from the manifest doi (as pages_apps.py already does) and keep it separate from the LabConstrictor citation; never hard-code the DOI text in the demo.

Reuse one folder of stamped frames for the demo, the docs 'run an example' tutorial and the video; align the demo with the App Centre inputs/outputs/quickstart/screenshots fields so it is the rich version of a pattern, not a bespoke page. Ask NucleiSky's authors to add the real frames to their manifest screenshots.

Make the design-rule change narrow and tested: a data-demo root, native controls only, tab/stepper semantics and a honesty-notice check; never relax button/alt checks globally. Decide a JS/CSS size budget in DESIGN.md.
Run the 5-biologist test with the pre-registered pass/fail thresholds in the findings, including a tile-only control and one phone participant; treat any Q3 or Q5 misreading as a blocker.
Fix the existing Welcome-picture alt text on the Use hub (the button is blue, not orange) before reusing the image.
Flip site visibility (extra.listed) as an explicit launch decision tied to Gate G1, not as a side effect.
